facts.fact: The supervising ministry's technical adviser Pape Ngor Thiaw said on 29 June 2026 that the NEKKAL programme had interconnected 400 civil-status centres and supplied centres with 1,200 computers and 1,000 printers; a count interconnected and equipped, with no total and not stated as a count registering digitally.
facts.system: système d'information de l'état civil (programme NEKKAL)

facts.fact: The NEKKAL programme supporting the civil-status information system was financed by the European Union and executed by Civipol and Enabel with ANEC, and held its final steering committee on 29 June 2026; the EU ambassador said the EU remained willing to support a consolidation phase.
facts.system: système d'information de l'état civil (programme NEKKAL)

facts.fact: By 29 June 2026 the programme had brought the validation of a Stratégie nationale de l'état civil as the sector's reference framework, of a draft law on computerising the management of civil-status events with its implementing decree, and of a study on the financing of civil status, per the ministry's adviser; the law is a validated draft, not an enacted text.
facts.system: système d'information de l'état civil (programme NEKKAL)

facts.fact: At the programme's final steering committee on 29 June 2026 the ministry reported 400 centres interconnected, a services platform in place, more than 4,000 civil-status actors trained and 26 modern centres built.
facts.system: système d'information de l'état civil (programme NEKKAL)
